sentences.text: The transformed algebra is always a weak algebra:
its operations are defined at most where their domain conditions hold.
There is a simple criterion for it to be an E P algebra.
Take an algebra with a single sort and two constants, zero and one.
A first derivor selects only zero, and interprets a unary operation u by the constant one.
Then u is nowhere defined, because one is not a cell.
A second derivor selects the points where u is defined, and nothing is left; but the composite derivor still keeps zero.
So there is only a natural inclusion of the composite of the induced functors into the functor induced by the composite, and the induced functors form a normal lax indexed category.
